description.narrative:
Detta projektstöd till SweFOR:s skyddsprogram syftar till att influera säkerhetsriskerna för människorättsförsvarare genom att: (i) Förhindra hot mot människorättsförsvarare; (ii) Minska människorättsförsvarares utsatthet; (iii) Öka skyddskapaciteten hos försvararnas organisationer för självskydd; och (iv) Öka den institutionella reaktionen för att skydda människorättsförsvarare. SweFOR har tre arbetsområden för att uppnå dessa mål:
1) Fysisk ledsagning av försvarare. 2) Öka graden av engagemang hos skyldighetsbärare och nyckelaktörer för skyddet av människorättsförsvarare. 3) Stärka självskyddssystem/mekanismer och kulturen för icke-våldsamt och differentierat självskydd.
Detta stöd är en fortsättning på ett tidigare projekt med ID-nummer: 12314.

This project support to SweFOR’s protection programme aims to influence the security risks of human rights defenders by: (i) Deterring threats to human rights defenders; (ii) Reducing vulnerability conditions of human rights defenders; (iii) Increasing protection capacities of defenders’ organisations for self-protection; and (iv) Increasing institutional reaction to protect human rights defenders. SweFOR has three working areas through which it will accomplish these goals:
1) Physical accompaniment to defenders. 2) Increasing the level of commitment of duty bearers and key stakeholders in the protection of Human Rights defenders. 3) Strengthen self-protection systems/mechanisms and the culture of non-violent and differentiated self-protection.
This contribution is a continuation of a previous project with ID-number: 12314.

description.narrative:
Note 14 April 2025: The results will be updated with 2024 data once annual partner reporting is submitted. The results below reflect the latest available data for 2023.
In 2023, SweFOR conducted 645 days of protective accompaniment, exceeding its target by 45 days. A total of 164 individuals from 10 organizations were accompanied, representing an increase from 2022 (105 individuals from 8 organizations). Of those accompanied, 101 were women and 23% were of Afro-Colombian descent. Partner organizations highlighted the positive impact of SweFORs presence, noting enhanced security and increased legitimacy with both regional and national stakeholders, which in turn strengthened their ability to influence change.
SweFOR also conducted 19 self-protection and security workshops with 30 different organizations, with 65% of participants being women and 28% Afro-descendants.
A key milestone from 2022 was the opening of a permanent office in Villavicencio, which enabled SweFOR to expand its presence further in 2023 to departments such as Casanare. In these new areas, efforts focused on building dialogue and communication channels with local actors, including the public force and the regional ombudsman, thereby raising awareness and visibility of SweFORs mission.
Additionally, in 2023, SweFOR revised its internal procedures and adapted its working methods to be more agile and responsive to the evolving needs of human rights defenders. This allowed the organization to increase its capacity to provide accompaniment in a more efficient and time-sensitive manner.
No indicator available - only a description of the activity results is published
